To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the CCVAE captures label characteristics in a way that allows for more effective interventions and that (ii) the CCVAEs can be trained in a variety of supervision regimes, from simple one-hot labels to more complex supervision, such as structured data.

(1) VAEs can be used to capture label characteristics, (2) this can be accomplished by reparameterizing supervision, and (3) the resulting representations can be manipulated to perform various interventions.

(a) we present the characteristic capturing V AE (CCVAE) that captures the characteristic information associated with labels in a principled manner, (b) we show that the latent variables in a CCVAE can be used to generate diverse conditional samples, and to perform smooth traversals within label characteristics, and (c) we show that CCVAE can transfer the characteristics across datapoints.

supervision in VAE-like models should be treated as a source of information about characteristics of interest, rather than a source of labels.
supervision in VAE can be used to capture label characteristics, and not simply the values of labels, which is useful for a variety of downstream tasks.
